name: Budget English Auctions
summary: Over 8 rounds, players with fixed coin budgets bid for items whose value only they can see, in short ascending auctions of up to 3 simultaneous bidding steps; the winner has the highest total of value minus price.

player.meaning: Coins left to bid with. Unspent coins carry over between rounds.
Total of (value - price) over all items won. It may be negative.
The player's own private deck of value cards still to come. The next card is drawn from it at random, so its order is secret.
The player's private value for this round's item, which is the card drawn this round.
Whether the player is still in this round's auction.
The player's raise in the current bidding step. 0 means DROP or not asked.
Scratch number used to pick the highest raise and break ties: raise*10000 + (500 - score)*10 - ((seat - start_seat + n) mod n), or 0 if the player did not raise.

game.meaning: The seat that tie-breaks count from this round: ((round-1) mod n)+1.
The current standing bid in this round's auction.
The seat of the current leader. 0 means there is no leader.
The current bidding step within the round, from 1 to 3.
Whether this round's bidding is still going on.
The value of the leader who bought the item this round, announced at settlement. 0 if the item went unsold.

setup: Each player gets coins = 40 and score = 0. Both are public.
Each player's private deck is set to the list [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16]. Cards are later drawn from it at random, which keeps the order secret and has the same effect as a separate shuffle.

round.effect: round += 1; start_seat = ((round-1) mod n)+1; standing_bid = 0; leader = 0; step = 0; bidding_open = true; revealed_value = 0; for every player: active = true, raise = 0, priority = 0; for every player: draw one card at random from their deck, set value to it and remove it from deck.
Each player privately sees their own value, coins and score, along with all public coins and scores.
All messages are collected at once and then broadcast {"to": "all", "text": "Seat {seat} says: {value}"}. Messages are not binding and change no state.
BIDDING STEP START (when bidding_open): step += 1; every active player who is not the leader and has coins < standing_bid + 2 gets active = false (forced drop); raise = 0 and priority = 0 for all.

round.who: every active player whose seat is not leader (when bidding_open)
round.answer: DROP, or a whole number from standing_bid + 2 to their coins
round.effect: Answers are gathered at once, and nobody sees another's answer until all are in. On DROP: active = false and raise = 0. On a number: raise = that number, and the player stays active.

(when bidding_open) For every player with raise > 0: priority = raise*10000 + (500 - score)*10 - ((seat - start_seat + n) mod n). If any raise > 0: standing_bid = max raise, and leader = the seat with the highest priority (highest raise, then lowest score, then the first seat counting upward from start_seat). Outbid raisers remain active. If no player has raise > 0: bidding_open = false. If step = 3: bidding_open = false.
Announce step, standing_bid, leader (or 'no leader') and the seats that dropped this step.
Repeat from BIDDING STEP START (the update, poll, update and tell steps) until bidding_open = false. This happens at the latest after step 3.

When leader > 0: the leader's coins -= standing_bid; the leader's score += (leader's value - standing_bid); revealed_value = the leader's value. When leader = 0, nothing changes and the item is unsold.
If leader > 0: 'Seat {leader} buys for {standing_bid}; their value was {revealed_value}.' Otherwise: 'The item goes unsold.' No other value is revealed.
If round >= 8, end the game. Otherwise continue to the next round. Unspent coins carry over.

ending.decided_by: The highest score (total of value minus price over items won) wins. A tie on score is broken by more coins remaining. Players still tied share the win, which is a draw among them.

rules.text: When the game starts, then every player has coins = 40 and score = 0, both public.
When the game starts, then each player's private deck holds exactly the cards 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16.
When a round starts, then each player draws one card from their own deck as their private value, the deck shrinks by one, and after 8 rounds every card has been used exactly once.
When a round starts, then standing_bid = 0, leader = 0 and every player is active.
When the talk step runs, then every player sends one message at the same time, and all messages are shown to everyone afterwards with no effect on state.
When a bidding step runs, then only active players who are not the leader are asked, all at the same time, to RAISE or DROP.
When a player raises, then the raise is a whole number of at least standing_bid + 2 and at most their coins (e.g. with standing_bid 6 and coins 10, only 8, 9 or 10 is allowed).
When an active non-leader has coins < standing_bid + 2 at the start of a step, then they are forced to drop and are not asked.
When a player drops, then they are out of this round's auction (active = false) and are not asked again this round.
When the leader exists during a step, then the leader is not asked and stays in.
When at least one player raised in a step, then standing_bid becomes the highest raise and its bidder becomes the leader.
When two or more players tie for the highest raise, then the one with the lowest score becomes leader.
When tied raisers also tie on score, then the leader is the first of them counting upward from seat ((r-1) mod n)+1, wrapping around (e.g. in round 2 with 4 seats, seat 2 beats seat 1).
When a player raised but was outbid, then they remain active for the next step.
When a step resolves, then the standing bid, the leader and the seats that dropped are announced.
When nobody raises in a step, then bidding ends immediately.
When step 3 has resolved, then bidding ends.
When bidding ends with a leader, then the leader pays standing_bid from coins and their score changes by (value - standing_bid), e.g. value 6 bought at 10 gives score -4.
When bidding ends with a leader, then the leader's value is announced and no other player's value is revealed.
When nobody raised during the round, then the item is unsold and no coins or scores change.
When a round ends, then unspent coins carry over to the next round.
When round 8 has settled, then the game ends.
When the game ends, then the highest score wins, ties go to more remaining coins, and players still tied share the win as a draw.

offers.question: Bidding step: RAISE or DROP
offers.who: every active seat that is not the leader and has coins >= standing_bid + 2
offers.options: DROP, or a whole number from standing_bid + 2 to that seat's coins

offers.question: Bidding step
offers.who: an active non-leader seat with coins < standing_bid + 2

offers.question: Bidding step
offers.who: a seat that dropped earlier this round

choices.why: The designer's suggested size of 4 is kept. The minimum is 3 because an auction needs at least two rivals for a bidder, so that the tie-breaks and the budget pressure matter. The maximum stays at 5 because with more seats one player's bids rarely decide an item and the talk becomes long.

choices.what: Talk kept as a simultaneous poll broadcast to all
choices.why: The source requires simultaneous messages. Talk earns its place because players disagree about who should win each item and can bluff about their values or signal restraint, and none of it is binding.

A thoughtful player bids below their value, saves coins for high-value rounds since the deck's remaining cards are known to them, reads rivals' coins and messages, and uses the 3-step limit to jump-bid. A thoughtless player overpays early or drops good items.

choices.what: Tie-break encoded as a priority number
choices.why: The priority raise*10000 + (500 - score)*10 - ((seat - start_seat + n) mod n) orders by highest raise, then lowest score, then seat order from start_seat. Scores stay within about -40 to 128, so the terms never overlap.
Coins never exceed 40, so coins act only as a tie-break after score, as the source states.

choices.what: Forced drop applied at the start of each step
choices.why: The source says such a player must drop. Applying it before the poll means they are never offered a choice they cannot make.

choices.what: Card values given as card_min_value 2, card_value_step 2 and card_max_value 16
choices.why: Parameters must be single numbers. The deck 2, 4, ..., 16 is every value from the minimum to the maximum in steps of 2, which is 8 cards (deck_size).

simplifications.what: The secretly shuffled deck is modelled as random draws without replacement from the player's deck list
simplifications.why: This is equivalent to drawing in order from a separately shuffled deck, and the order stays secret even from its owner.

simplifications.what: The 3 bidding steps are a repeated block of four steps that stops when bidding_open becomes false
simplifications.why: The engine runs steps in a flat list with repeat. A step where nobody raises, or step 3, closes the bidding.
